answer: On a karst ridge, each surveyor owns one stone vertex pillar and files a dated star chart from it each month, naming the nebula visible above the ridge that night. A roving checker re-reads every tenth pillar and voids any chart whose nebula does not match the sky on that date, and a second pillar under one name voids both claims for a season. To run a thousand fake surveyors, an attacker must raise a thousand pillars, file a thousand monthly charts, and pass a thousand re-reads against the real night sky.
